title: Time-dependent attenuation of transgenerational immune effects in HIV-positive mothers: circular and linear RNA dynamics
description: The primary goal of this study was to investigate the time-dependent dynamics of transgenerational immune responses in HIV-positive mothers. To do so, we collected peripheral blood samples from 466 pregnant women in South Africa. We also followed their offspring and collected peripheral blood samples at birth, at one year of age, and again at five years of age. We performed group comparison between mothers that were once HIV-positive but cured and healthy controls. For offspring data of each timepoint, we performed group comparison between children born to mothers with a history of HIV infection and those born to mothers unexposed to HIV. By performing the gene differential expression analysis from both the aspect of linear RNA and circular RNA, we coincidently observed that while children born to the HIV-infected mothers showed a higher level of immune response compared to those born to by HIV non-infected mothers, this transgenerational effect decreased gradually as children grew up.
